I read the image only. Parts of it are ambiguous, and I say where.

1. The animation is about inflation eroding a fixed payment. It uses US consumer prices (CPI-U) from Aug 2006 to Aug 2026 as an illustration. It compares a "level check," which stays the same dollar amount, with a "rising check," which grows over time. The upper line is labelled "first check."

2. In frame 1, the upper line is drawn first and wanders near the "first check" level, then slips lower toward the end. In frame 2, a second line, the "level check," falls steadily and ends well below the first. In frame 3, a marker at year 5 shows the level check at about 9 in 10 of its starting value. In frame 4, a marker at year 20 shows the rising check reaching the height the level check had at year 5. Frames 5 and 6 add a "?" and hold the same picture.

3. A payment that never rises buys less each year. By year 5 it buys about 90% of what it did at the start, and by year 20 it buys much less. A payment that rises takes about 20 years to get back to where the level check stood at year 5. The "?" suggests the trade-off is left open. I'm unsure exactly how the rising check is meant to compare with the first check, because the wording is terse. The footer says "US only · history, not a forecast," and the "ILLUSTRATIVE" tag says the numbers aren't a quote.

4. The animation gives no explicit advice. A viewer could take away that inflation matters when comparing a level payout with a rising one. They might also take away that the rising option starts out costing something and only pays off over a long horizon.

5. That takeaway is my own conclusion. The animation only shows the lines and labels and tells the viewer nothing about what to choose.
